prompt: In Tennessee, a driver age 21 or older is driving under the influence per se at what blood or breath alcohol concentration?
explanation: Tennessee law makes it unlawful to drive with an alcohol concentration of .08 percent or higher. Drivers can still be charged below that level if they are impaired.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 95

prompt: A Tennessee driver's breath test shows .05 percent, but the officer saw them weaving across lanes. Which statement is correct?
choices: They cannot be charged because they are under .08
They can only be charged if the BAC rises later
They can still be convicted of DUI if alcohol impaired their driving
Only drivers under 21 can be charged below .08
explanation: The manual says a BAC below .08 does not clear a driver; a person can even register .00 and still be convicted of DUI if impaired by alcohol or drugs.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 95

prompt: A 19-year-old Tennessee driver is caught driving with a BAC of .02 percent. What is this offense called?
choices: Nothing, because .02 is below the legal limit
explanation: Drivers who are at least 16 but not yet 21 and are found driving with a BAC of .02 percent are convicted of underage driving while impaired.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 97

prompt: What are the penalties for a conviction of underage driving while impaired in Tennessee?
choices: A written warning for a first offense
Loss of license for 30 days and a $50 fine
Loss of license for one year, a $250 fine and sometimes public service work
explanation: Underage driving while impaired (BAC of .02 for ages 16-20) brings loss of license for one year, a $250 fine and sometimes public service work.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 97

prompt: Under Tennessee's implied consent law, what will likely happen if you are arrested for DUI and refuse the officer's request to take a test?
choices: A suspension of your driving privileges by the court for 12 months
A fine only, with no effect on your license
explanation: By driving in Tennessee you have consented to testing. Refusing after arrest will likely result in the court suspending your driving privileges for twelve months.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 95

prompt: What is the minimum jail time for a first DUI conviction in Tennessee when the driver's BAC was below 0.20 percent?
explanation: A first DUI conviction carries at least 48 hours in jail. If the BAC was 0.20 percent or more, the minimum rises to 7 days.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 96

prompt: How long is a driver's license revoked for a first DUI conviction in Tennessee?
explanation: The manual's DUI penalty table lists a 1-year license revocation for a first conviction and 2 years for a second.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 96

prompt: What fine range applies to a first DUI conviction in Tennessee?
explanation: A first DUI conviction carries a fine of $350 to $1,500. The $600-$3,500 range applies to a second conviction.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 96

prompt: Besides fines and jail, what must every person convicted of DUI in Tennessee do as a condition of probation?
choices: Pick up litter for three eight-hour shifts while wearing clothing that says "I am a DRUNK DRIVER"
Display a special license plate for one year
Retake the road test before driving again
Attend a court-ordered victim panel every week for a year
explanation: Tennessee requires litter pickup for three eight-hour shifts while wearing a vest or clothing that reads "I am a DRUNK DRIVER."
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 95

prompt: A driver is convicted of DUI while a 10-year-old child was riding in the car. What extra penalty does Tennessee's Drunk Driving Child Protection Act add?
choices: A mandatory minimum of 30 days in jail and a $1,000 minimum fine
An extra 48 hours in jail only
A warning letter to the child's school
No extra penalty unless the child was injured
explanation: DUI with a passenger under 18 adds a mandatory minimum 30-day jail sentence and a mandatory minimum $1,000 fine on top of other penalties.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 96

prompt: A 20-year-old in Tennessee is convicted of possessing beer while walking home, not driving. What happens to their driving privilege?
choices: Nothing, because they were not driving
They lose it for one year
They receive 3 points on their record
explanation: Drivers aged 18, 19 or 20 convicted of buying, trying to buy or possessing alcohol lose their privilege to drive for one year, whether or not they were driving.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 97

prompt: A 14-year-old in Tennessee who has never been licensed is found in possession of alcohol. How does this affect their future driving privilege?
choices: It has no effect because they have no license
It is suspended for one year or until age 17, whichever is longer
They must wait until age 21 to get a license
explanation: For ages 13-17, possessing, consuming or selling alcohol or drugs suspends the driving privilege for one year or until age 17, whichever is longer, even if never licensed.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 97

prompt: By Tennessee law, at least what share of the questions on the driver knowledge test must deal with alcohol and drugs?
explanation: Tennessee law requires at least 25 percent of the knowledge test questions to deal with drinking or drugs and driving.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 93

prompt: Under Tennessee's 2019 hands-free law, which action is illegal for an adult driver while driving?
choices: Using a hands-free earpiece for a call
Holding a cell phone with any part of their body
Using a voice command that needs no touching
explanation: Public Chapter 412 makes it illegal for a driver to hold a cellphone or mobile device with any part of their body, among other things.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 44

prompt: You are driving in Tennessee and want to change the destination in your phone's GPS app. What should you do?
choices: Hold the phone low in your lap so police cannot see it
Pull over safely and stop before using the phone
Type the address only while stopped at a red light
Use it quickly at speeds under 25 mph
explanation: The manual says you are not allowed to touch your phone to use GPS while driving; find a safe place to pull over, stop, and then use it. Set navigation before you start.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 6

prompt: A 35-year-old Tennessee driver reads an incoming text on a phone mounted on the dashboard while driving. Is this legal?
choices: Yes, because the phone is mounted and not held
Yes, because the texting ban applies only to drivers under 18
No, reading any text-based communication while driving is illegal for all drivers
No, but only inside school zones
explanation: Tennessee's hands-free law makes it illegal for any driver to write, send or read any text-based communication, even if the phone is mounted.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 44

prompt: A 16-year-old with a Tennessee intermediate license wants to take a call through the car's Bluetooth system while driving. Is this allowed?
choices: Yes, because hands-free calls are legal for everyone
No, permit and intermediate license holders may not use a cell phone at all while driving
No, unless a parent is on the call
explanation: Tennessee prohibits any driver with a learner permit or intermediate license from using a cell phone while driving (the definition includes car phones and other mobile phones), so the hands-free option allowed for adult drivers does not help.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 32

prompt: What are the consequences when a Tennessee teen with a learner permit is convicted of using a cell phone while driving?
choices: A $50 fine, 6 points, and a 90-day delay in eligibility for the Intermediate Restricted license
Immediate loss of the permit until age 18
explanation: The conviction is a Class C misdemeanor with a $50 fine, 6 points on the minor's record and a 90-day delay in eligibility for the Intermediate Restricted license.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 32

prompt: An adult driver in Tennessee is moving through a marked school zone while its warning flashers are operating. Which phone use is allowed?
choices: Holding the phone for a short call
Using the phone in hands-free mode
Reading a text at low speed
Holding the phone to check directions
explanation: It is an offense for drivers 18 or older to use a hand-held phone while moving in a marked school zone when flashers are operating; hands-free mode is the exception for adults.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 44

prompt: Who must wear a safety belt any time a vehicle is moving in Tennessee?
choices: The driver and every front-seat passenger
explanation: Tennessee requires safety belts for all drivers and all front-seat passengers any time the vehicle is in motion, and officers can stop you for this alone.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 45

prompt: In Tennessee, a child who is under one year old or who weighs less than 20 pounds must ride in:
choices: A booster seat with a lap belt
An adult seat belt in the back seat
explanation: A child under one year old, or any child under 20 pounds, must be in a rear-facing child passenger restraint system.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 45

prompt: In Tennessee, a 6-year-old who is 4 feet 2 inches tall must ride:
choices: In a belt-positioning booster seat with a seat belt
With only the vehicle's lap and shoulder belt
In the front seat with the airbag off
explanation: Children four through eight years old who are shorter than 4 feet 9 inches must use a belt-positioning booster seat and wear a seat belt, in the back seat if the vehicle has one.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 45

prompt: In Tennessee, the driver is responsible for properly restraining child passengers up to what age?
explanation: The law makes the driver responsible for protecting children up to age 16; a driver can be fined $50 if children under 16 are not properly restrained.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 45

prompt: Under Tennessee law, may a 5-year-old ride in the bed of a pickup truck on a county road?
choices: Yes, if the truck stays under 35 mph
Yes, if an adult rides in the bed too
No, children under 6 may not ride in a pickup bed (except in parades or agricultural activities)
Yes, on any road other than an interstate
explanation: It is illegal to allow any child under 6 to ride in a pickup bed. The only exceptions are organized parades at 20 mph or less and agricultural activities.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 47

prompt: In Tennessee, it can be an offense to leave a child younger than what age in a vehicle in a public place without supervision by someone at least 13?
explanation: It is an offense to knowingly leave a child younger than 7 in a vehicle in a public place without a supervisor at least 13 if conditions are risky, the engine is running, or the keys are inside.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 47

prompt: What is the minimum age to get a Class PD learner permit in Tennessee?
explanation: You must be 15 years old and pass the knowledge test and vision screening to get a learner permit.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 28

prompt: How long must a Tennessee driver under 18 hold a learner permit before applying for an Intermediate Restricted license?
explanation: Drivers under 18 must hold the learner permit for 180 days (six months) before moving to the Intermediate Restricted license.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 28

prompt: How many hours of certified driving practice does a Tennessee teen need before getting an Intermediate Restricted license?
explanation: A parent, legal guardian or licensed driving instructor must certify 50 hours of driving experience, including 10 hours at night, on the official form.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 28

prompt: Who must be with a Tennessee learner permit holder when they drive?
choices: A licensed driver 21 or older riding in the front seat
A licensed driver of any age in the back seat
A parent only, in any seat
explanation: A learner permit holder may drive only when accompanied by a licensed driver 21 years or older who is riding in the front seat.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 28

prompt: During which hours may a Tennessee learner permit holder under 18 NOT drive, even with a supervisor?
explanation: Permit holders under 18 are prohibited from driving between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m. The 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. limit applies to the Intermediate Restricted license.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 28

prompt: What is the minimum age for a Tennessee Intermediate Restricted license?
explanation: You must be 16 and pass the road test, after holding the learner permit for 180 days.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 28

prompt: An Intermediate Restricted license holder in Tennessee may not drive between which hours unless an exception applies?
explanation: Intermediate Restricted drivers are prohibited from driving between 11 p.m. and 6 a.m. unless they meet an exception such as driving with a parent or going to or from work with written permission.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 33

prompt: A 16-year-old with a Tennessee Intermediate Restricted license wants to drive to a fishing spot at 4:30 a.m. When is this allowed?
choices: Never; the curfew has no exceptions
When they carry a valid hunting or fishing license
Only if they drive under 35 mph
explanation: One curfew exception is driving to or from hunting or fishing between 4 a.m. and 6 a.m. while carrying a valid hunting or fishing license.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 33

prompt: Without an exception, how many passengers may a Tennessee Intermediate Restricted license holder carry?
explanation: Intermediate Restricted drivers may have only 1 other passenger in the vehicle unless an exception applies.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 33

prompt: A Tennessee Intermediate Restricted driver wants to carry three friends. Which situation makes this legal?
choices: One of the passengers is 21 or older with a valid unrestricted license
explanation: The one-passenger limit does not apply when one or more passengers is 21 or older with a valid, unrestricted license (or when carrying siblings to and from school with a parent's letter).
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 33

prompt: To move up to a Tennessee Intermediate Unrestricted license, a teen must be at least 17 and have held the Intermediate Restricted license for how long?
explanation: The Intermediate Restricted license must be held for at least 1 year, and the driver must be 17.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 28

prompt: Which of these adds 90 days to the time a Tennessee teen must hold an Intermediate Restricted license?
choices: Being convicted of a second seat belt violation
explanation: A teen becomes ineligible for the Intermediate Unrestricted license for an extra 90 days for 6 or more points, contributing to a crash, or a second seat belt violation.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 33

prompt: What happens to a Tennessee Intermediate Restricted driver convicted of carrying a forged letter allowing them to drive after curfew?
choices: The license is revoked and only a learner permit is reissued until age 18
A 90-day delay before the next level
explanation: A forged or fraudulent permission letter leads to revocation of the Intermediate Restricted license; the driver is reissued only a learner permit until age 18.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 33

prompt: A 17-year-old in Tennessee graduates from high school. When can they get a regular Class D license?
choices: Now, because graduating from high school or getting a GED allows it before 18
Only after 2 more years of intermediate driving
explanation: A regular Class D license is available at 18 or when the driver graduates from high school or receives a GED, whichever is sooner.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 28

prompt: A Tennessee student drops out of school for the second time at age 16. When can they apply for a license again?
explanation: A first dropout can regain driving privileges by returning to school, but after a second dropout the student must wait until age 18.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 31

prompt: An adult Tennessee driver receives a notice of proposed suspension after collecting how many points within 12 months?
explanation: Adult drivers (18+) who accumulate 12 or more points within a 12-month period receive a notice of proposed suspension.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 100

prompt: A 17-year-old Tennessee driver collects 6 points within 12 months. What happens?
choices: They receive a notice of proposed suspension
They must retake the knowledge test only
explanation: Juvenile drivers (under 18) who accumulate 6 or more points in 12 months receive a notice of proposed suspension, half the adult threshold.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 100

prompt: What are Tennessee's minimum liability insurance limits?
choices: $25,000 per person, $50,000 per accident, $25,000 property damage
$15,000 per person, $30,000 per accident, $5,000 property damage
$50,000 per person, $100,000 per accident, $50,000 property damage
$30,000 per person, $60,000 per accident, $25,000 property damage
explanation: Tennessee requires at least $25,000 for each injury or death, $50,000 for total injuries or deaths per accident, and $25,000 for property damage.
ref: Tennessee Department of Revenue, Financial Responsibility Law (tn.gov/revenue)

prompt: When does Tennessee's Financial Responsibility Law require you to show evidence of insurance or other financial responsibility?
choices: Only when you renew your license
When charged with any violation or involved in a crash, regardless of fault
Only after a crash that you caused
explanation: Drivers must produce evidence of financial responsibility when charged with any violation or involved in a motor vehicle crash, without regard to fault.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 102

prompt: After you move to a new address, how soon must you notify the Tennessee Department of Safety?
explanation: State law requires you to notify the Department of Safety of an address change within ten days, even if the post office changed your address.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 27

prompt: If you fail the Tennessee driver knowledge test, when may you retake it?
explanation: A mandatory 1-day waiting period applies after failing any driver license knowledge test; no test may be repeated the same day.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 36

prompt: What is the maximum speed limit set by Tennessee law for interstate highways?
explanation: Tennessee law sets 70 mph as the interstate maximum, posted on most rural sections; congested urban interstates are typically 55 mph.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 61

prompt: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit on Tennessee's primary and secondary state and federal highways?
explanation: Unless another limit is posted, the speed limit on primary and secondary state and federal highways is 55 mph.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 61

prompt: You are driving at 50 mph in the left-most lane of a Tennessee interstate with light traffic. Why is this a problem?
choices: It is illegal to drive under 55 mph in the left-most lane unless congestion prevents it
The left lane is only for trucks
The minimum speed in every lane is 60 mph
There is no problem as long as you signal
explanation: Tennessee law makes it unlawful to drive under 55 mph in the left-most interstate lane unless traffic congestion and flow prevent safe driving at that speed.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 61

prompt: What is the minimum speed in the right lane(s) of a Tennessee interstate under normal conditions?
explanation: On interstates the minimum speed limit in the right lane(s) is 45 mph. If that is too fast for you, use another road.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 61

prompt: In Tennessee you are driving 15 mph below the speed limit on a two-lane road, and six vehicles are lined up behind you. What does the law expect?
choices: Speed up to the limit immediately
Turn or pull off the roadway as soon as you can do so safely
Turn on your hazard lights and keep going
explanation: Driving 10 mph or more below the maximum makes you a slow-moving vehicle; if five or more vehicles are lined up behind you, pull off when safe.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 60

prompt: In Tennessee, what is the legal consequence of exceeding the posted speed limit in a school zone?
choices: It is considered reckless driving and adds an automatic 6 points
It is a parking-type violation with no points
explanation: Exceeding the school zone speed limit is by law considered reckless driving, with an automatic six points and an advisory letter.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 61

prompt: What fine range does Tennessee law set for speeding in an active work zone?
explanation: Tennessee law mandates a minimum fine of $250 and up to $500 for violating the posted speed limit in active work zones.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 61

prompt: The Tennessee manual recommends a two-second following distance on roads with moderate speeds. When should you increase it to at least four seconds?
choices: Only when following a school bus
In bad weather, at night, at higher interstate speeds, and when following a motorcycle
Never; two seconds is enough at any speed
explanation: The two-second rule should be increased to a minimum of four seconds for inclement weather, higher-speed interstate driving, night driving and following a motorcycle.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 63

prompt: You reach an intersection in Tennessee where the traffic lights are completely dark because of a power outage. What must you do?
choices: Proceed at normal speed if you are on the larger road
Treat it as an all-way stop
Yield only to traffic on your left
explanation: Tennessee law requires that when a signal is not working, the intersection be treated as an all-way stop.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 55

prompt: Tennessee law requires a yellow traffic light to be shown for at least how long before the light turns red?
explanation: Tennessee law only requires the yellow light to be exhibited for a minimum of three seconds before the red, so prepare to stop when it appears.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 55

prompt: In Tennessee, when may you turn right on a steady red light?
choices: After a complete stop, when no pedestrians or cross traffic are present, unless a sign prohibits it
Without stopping, if no one is coming
Only when a green arrow is also lit
explanation: Unless otherwise posted, you may turn right on red after coming to a complete stop and when no pedestrians or cross traffic are present.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 55

prompt: In Tennessee, where is a left turn on a red light allowed (after a complete stop, unless posted otherwise)?
choices: From a one-way street onto another one-way street with traffic moving left
From a two-way street onto a one-way street
From a one-way street onto a two-way street
explanation: A left on red is permitted where a one-way street meets another one-way street and traffic moves in the direction of the turn.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 72

prompt: You are stopped at a red light on a one-way street and want to turn left onto a two-way street. What does Tennessee law say?
choices: You may turn after a full stop
You may turn if no traffic is coming
You cannot make this left turn on red
You may turn only after 10 p.m.
explanation: Turning left on red is allowed only onto another one-way street. When turning from a one-way street onto a two-way street, you cannot make the left turn on red.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 71

prompt: What is the longest distance you may travel in a shared center two-way left-turn lane in Tennessee?
explanation: Shared center turn lanes are reserved for left turns; they cannot be used for passing or for travel farther than 300 feet.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 74

prompt: How far before a turn does Tennessee require you to turn on your turn signal?
explanation: Tennessee drivers must signal at least 50 feet before turning or changing lanes.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 70

prompt: In Tennessee, a U-turn is NOT allowed at a location where you cannot see approaching traffic for at least how far in each direction?
explanation: You may not make a U-turn anywhere you cannot see traffic coming from both directions for at least 500 feet, such as near curves or hill crests.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 73

prompt: You missed your exit on a Tennessee interstate. Which choice is legal?
choices: Make a U-turn through an emergency crossover
Back up slowly on the shoulder
Drive on to the next exit
Cross the median when no traffic is near
explanation: It is illegal to back up or make a U-turn on an interstate, and emergency crossovers are only for emergency vehicles and highway maintenance crews. Drive on to the next exit.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, pp. 73, 84

prompt: A fire engine is approaching from behind with its siren on while you are stopped at a red light. The light turns green before the fire engine reaches you. What should you do?
choices: Go through on the green light to clear the way
Stay where you are until the emergency vehicle has passed
Turn right on red to get out of the way
explanation: The manual says if the light is red, stay where you are, and if it turns green before the emergency vehicle passes, do NOT proceed until it has passed or turned.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 68

prompt: Under Tennessee law, what must you do when an emergency vehicle with a siren or flashing lights approaches?
choices: Speed up to stay ahead of it
Pull parallel to and close to the right edge or curb and stop until it passes
Move to the left lane and keep driving
explanation: All traffic meeting or being overtaken must yield and immediately drive close to the right-hand edge or curb and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 68

prompt: A fire engine has stopped to handle an emergency on a city street. What does Tennessee law forbid?
choices: Driving your vehicle within the block where it has stopped
Driving on the next street over
Slowing down as you pass the next intersection
explanation: It is illegal to follow an emergency vehicle answering a call or to take your vehicle within the block where it has stopped. Do not drive over fire hoses without permission.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 68

prompt: A fire truck is backing into the driveway of a fire station ahead of you. What should you do?
explanation: When approaching a fire station, yield to any emergency vehicle about to back into, or already backing into, the station's driveway entrance.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 67

prompt: In a Tennessee school zone with the warning flashers operating, a pedestrian starts across the road in a crosswalk ahead. What must you do?
choices: Slow down and pass behind the pedestrian
Stop and remain stopped until the pedestrian has crossed the roadway you are on
Honk and continue if the pedestrian is not in your lane
Stop only if a crossing guard signals
explanation: In a marked school zone with flashers operating, the driver must stop for a pedestrian crossing in a crosswalk and stay stopped until the pedestrian has crossed the roadway.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 67

prompt: A pedestrian carrying a white cane is crossing the road in Tennessee. What should you do?
choices: Honk to let them know where you are
Stop at least 10 feet away until they are off the roadway, without honking
explanation: For a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, stop at least 10 feet away until the person is off the roadway, and do not use your horn.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 67

prompt: Is it illegal in Tennessee to pass more than one vehicle at a time on a two-lane road?
choices: Yes, passing more than one vehicle at a time is always illegal
No, but it is generally unsafe and should be considered only on a straight, level road with excellent visibility
Yes, unless you sound your horn first
No, and it is just as safe as passing a single vehicle
explanation: Passing multiple vehicles is not illegal in Tennessee but, as a general rule, is not safe. Only consider it on a straight, level road where you can be back in the right lane before coming within 100 feet of no-passing markings or oncoming vehicles.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 76

prompt: You are behind a properly identified funeral procession on a two-lane road in Tennessee. What does the law say?
choices: You may pass if the procession is slower than 25 mph
You may not attempt to pass the procession
You may join the line between vehicles
explanation: Tennessee law says vehicles following a funeral procession on a two-lane roadway may not pass it, and no one may drive between vehicles in the procession unless directed by an officer.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 60

prompt: In Tennessee, how close to a fire hydrant may you park?
explanation: It is illegal to park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 79

prompt: In Tennessee, it is illegal to park within how many feet of a crosswalk?
explanation: Do not park within 20 feet of a crosswalk or in the marked crosswalk area.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 79

prompt: In Tennessee, you may not park within how many feet of a stop sign or traffic signal?
explanation: It is illegal to park within 30 feet of a traffic signal, stop sign or any other traffic control device.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 79

prompt: In Tennessee, you may not park within how many feet of a railroad crossing?
explanation: Parking within 50 feet of a railroad crossing is illegal. (15 feet is the fire hydrant distance.)
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 79

prompt: You want to park across the street from a fire station driveway in Tennessee. How far from the driveway must you be?
explanation: Do not park within 20 feet of a fire station driveway on the same side of the street, or within 75 feet of it on the other side of the street.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 79

prompt: After you finish parallel parking in Tennessee, your vehicle should be no farther than how far from the curb?
explanation: Upon completing a parallel parking maneuver, the vehicle should be no farther away from the curb than 18 inches.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 80

prompt: When you park beside a road outside city limits in Tennessee, how much road width must you leave for other traffic?
explanation: Get all four wheels off the pavement if possible, and always leave at least 18 feet of road width for traffic. Your vehicle must also be visible for 200 feet in each direction.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 79

prompt: On a Tennessee interstate, you approach a police car stopped on the right shoulder with lights flashing. If it is safe, what does the Move Over law require?
choices: Slow down by 5 mph and stay in your lane
Change into a lane that is not next to the stopped vehicle
explanation: When safety and traffic allow, you must move into a lane not adjacent to the stationary emergency vehicle. Slowing down and staying in your lane is allowed only when a lane change is unsafe.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 86

prompt: Heavy traffic makes it unsafe to change lanes when you approach a stopped tow truck with flashing lights on a Tennessee multi-lane highway. What should you do?
choices: Stop in your lane until it leaves
Proceed with caution, reduce speed and keep a safe speed for conditions
Drive onto the left shoulder to get away
Continue at normal speed because you cannot move over
explanation: Only when a lane change is impossible or unsafe may you stay in your lane, and then you must proceed with due caution and reduce your speed.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 86

prompt: Does Tennessee's Move Over law apply when an ordinary car with its hazard flashers on is stopped on the shoulder of a four-lane highway?
choices: No, it applies only to police, fire and ambulances
Yes, it now applies to any stationary motor vehicle displaying flashing lights
Only if the car has a flat tire
explanation: The law now applies to all stationary motor vehicles with emergency flashers on when you are on a highway with at least four lanes and two going your direction.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 86

prompt: A highway maintenance truck with flashing lights is stopped on the LEFT shoulder of a Tennessee interstate. What does the Move Over law require when it is safe?
choices: Nothing, because the law covers only the right shoulder
Merge into the right lane, leaving the left-most lane open
Move onto the left shoulder behind it
Speed up to pass it quickly
explanation: The move-over requirement applies on either side of the road. If the vehicle is on the left shoulder, merge right to free the left-most lane as a safety barrier.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 86

prompt: You have a minor crash on a Tennessee interstate. The cars can still be driven and no one is seriously hurt. What does Tennessee law allow?
choices: Leave the scene and report it online later
Move the vehicles to the emergency lane and wait for police there
Leave the vehicles in the travel lanes until police arrive
Drive to the next exit without telling anyone
explanation: Tennessee's Move It for Safety rule lets you move drivable vehicles to the emergency lane when there are no serious injuries or deaths, then wait for an officer. You must not leave the scene.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 87

prompt: What number can you dial free from a cell phone to reach the nearest Tennessee Highway Patrol dispatcher during a highway emergency?
explanation: Dialing *THP (*847) connects you at no charge to the nearest Tennessee Highway Patrol Dispatch Center.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 87

prompt: During the posted rush-hour periods, which of these vehicles may use a Tennessee interstate HOV lane?
choices: A car with only the driver
A driver alone who is passing slower traffic
A pickup towing a trailer with one person
explanation: During HOV hours, the lane is reserved for vehicles with two or more people, buses, emergency vehicles, and motorcycles occupied by one person. Solo drivers may not use it, even to pass.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 83

prompt: In Tennessee, you must immediately notify police of a crash involving death, injury, or property damage over what amount?
explanation: Drivers must immediately notify the local police, sheriff or Highway Patrol of any crash involving death, injury or property damage over $50.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 103

prompt: When must a Tennessee driver file an Owner/Driver crash report with the Department of Safety and Homeland Security?
choices: Within 20 days after a crash with injury, death or more than $400 property damage
Within 10 days, only if a police officer did not come
Only if the other driver was uninsured
explanation: Reportable crashes (any injury or death, or more than $400 damage to one person's property) require an Owner/Driver Report within 20 days, regardless of who was at fault.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 103

prompt: You back into a fence and cause about $600 in damage, with no injuries. Under Tennessee rules, is this a reportable crash?
choices: No, only crashes with injuries are reportable
Yes, because damage to one person's property is over $400
No, because only one vehicle was involved
Only if the fence owner calls police
explanation: A crash is any collision with another vehicle, person or object. Damage over $400 to any one person's property makes it reportable to the Department within 20 days.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 103

prompt: You knowingly drive around a "Road Closed" barricade onto a flooded road in Tennessee and must be rescued. What can happen?
choices: Nothing, because flooding is an act of nature
You can be charged with reckless driving and made to repay the cost of your rescue
Your insurance automatically pays the rescue cost
explanation: Knowingly ignoring flood warning signs or barricades and driving into a flooded road can bring a reckless driving charge and responsibility for the cost of your rescue.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 91

prompt: On a two-lane road in Tennessee, a school bus stopped in the opposite lane has its red lights flashing and stop arm out. What must you do?
choices: Stop and stay stopped until the stop arm is pulled back and the bus moves
Stop only if children are visible
Continue, because only traffic behind the bus must stop
explanation: Drivers meeting a school or church bus with red lights flashing must stop and remain stopped until the stop arm is pulled back and the bus resumes motion.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 65

prompt: On a five-lane Tennessee road with a center turn lane, a school bus stops on the other side with red lights flashing. Must you stop?
choices: No, the center turn lane counts as a barrier
Yes, a center turn lane is not a barrier, so traffic in both directions must stop
Only if you are in the lane nearest the bus
No, school bus laws apply only to two-lane roads
explanation: A turn lane in the middle of a four-lane highway is not considered a barrier, so drivers in both directions must stop. Only a median or barrier not suitable for vehicles exempts oncoming traffic.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 65

prompt: You are on a Tennessee divided highway with a grass median. A school bus stopped on the other side of the median has its red lights flashing. What should you do?
choices: You need not stop, but proceed with caution
Stop only if children are crossing
Pull onto the shoulder and wait
explanation: On a highway with separate roadways divided by a median or barrier not suitable for vehicles, the driver need not stop but should proceed with caution.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 65

prompt: What fine range does Tennessee set for failing to stop for a stopped school bus?
explanation: Not stopping for a stopped school bus is a Class A misdemeanor with a fine between $250 and $1,000. Passing a stopped school, church or youth bus also adds 8 points to your record.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, pp. 65, 101

prompt: Which vehicles must stop at every Tennessee railroad crossing, even when no signals are active?
choices: School and church buses, vehicles carrying passengers for hire, and vehicles hauling flammables or explosives
explanation: Church or school buses (even empty), common carriers carrying passengers for hire, and vehicles carrying flammables, explosives or other dangerous cargo must stop at every crossing.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 65

prompt: A train is approaching a Tennessee railroad crossing. Where must you stop?
choices: Between 5 and 10 feet from the tracks
Between 15 and 50 feet from the tracks
At least 100 feet from the tracks
Directly on the stop line, even if it is on the tracks
explanation: When a train is coming, you must stop between 15 and 50 feet from the railroad tracks and never on the tracks.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 64

prompt: When passing a bicyclist going the same direction, how much space does Tennessee law require?
explanation: Pass a bicyclist slowly and leave at least 3 feet of distance, keeping that clearance until you are safely past.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 77

prompt: During which hours does Tennessee law require you to use your headlights?
choices: From 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise
From 1 hour after sunset until 1 hour before sunrise
explanation: Headlights must be on from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, and at other times when visibility is poor.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 59

prompt: It is daytime in Tennessee, and light rain requires your windshield wipers to run constantly. What does the law say about headlights?
explanation: Tennessee law requires headlights whenever rain, mist, snow or other precipitation requires constant use of windshield wipers.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 59

prompt: When must you dim your high beams for an oncoming vehicle in Tennessee?
explanation: Dim your high beams when an oncoming vehicle is within 500 feet, about one city block.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 59

prompt: You are following another vehicle at night in Tennessee. Within what distance must you switch from high to low beams?
explanation: Tennessee also requires dimming when you are following another vehicle within 500 feet; glare in the mirror can blind the driver ahead.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 59

prompt: The posted limit on a two-lane Tennessee highway is 65 mph, but it is night and foggy. What does the Basic Speed Rule in the Tennessee manual say?
choices: You may drive 65 mph because that is the posted limit
65 mph may be too fast; your speed must be reasonable for current conditions
You must drive exactly 10 mph under the posted limit
You must keep at least 55 mph so you do not block traffic
explanation: The Basic Speed Rule is a general safety principle, not a Tennessee law: your safe speed is limited by current conditions. The manual's own example says 65 mph is too fast on a two-lane highway at night in rain or fog.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 60

prompt: According to the Tennessee manual, how are speed limits on residential roads and city streets set?
choices: They vary and are posted; some are as low as 25 or 35 mph at all times
Tennessee has one statewide residential limit of 40 mph
They always match the 55 mph default for state highways
They apply only during school hours
explanation: The state, counties and cities each set limits on roads they control, and some residential roads or city streets have limits as low as 25 or 35 mph at all times. Watch for and obey the posted signs.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 61

prompt: Assuming no signs or other restrictions apply, which of these is a place where Tennessee law prohibits parking?
explanation: Parking within an intersection is always illegal. The other spots are outside Tennessee's no-parking distances: 20 feet from a crosswalk, 30 feet from a stop sign and 15 feet from a fire hydrant.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 79

prompt: Under Tennessee law, who must wear a crash helmet on a motorcycle?
explanation: Tennessee requires every person operating or riding a motorcycle to wear a crash helmet meeting federal standard 49 CFR 571.218. Riders 21+ may use certain other labeled helmets.
ref: Tennessee Motorcycle Operator Manual, p. 23

prompt: When may a Tennessee motorcycle rider legally ride without a helmet?
choices: When 18 or older in a parade at no more than 30 mph
On roads with speed limits under 35 mph
explanation: The only exemption is for riders 18 or older on a motorcycle ridden in a parade at a speed not exceeding 30 mph.
ref: Tennessee Motorcycle Operator Manual, p. 24

prompt: Is lane splitting (riding between lanes or rows of vehicles) legal in Tennessee?
explanation: Tennessee law (Tenn. Code Ann. 55-8-182) says no person shall operate a motorcycle between lanes of traffic or between rows of vehicles.
ref: Tennessee Motorcycle Operator Manual, p. 25

prompt: In Tennessee, what is the most motorcycles that may ride side by side in a single lane?
explanation: Motorcycles shall not be operated more than two abreast in a single lane. A motorcycle may not pass in the same lane as the vehicle it is overtaking.
ref: Tennessee Motorcycle Operator Manual, p. 25

prompt: A Tennessee motorcycle has no windshield. What eye protection must the operator and passenger use?
choices: Safety goggles or glasses with impact-resistant lenses, or a helmet with a face shield
explanation: Motorcycles must have a DOT-compliant windshield; otherwise operators and passengers must wear impact-resistant goggles or glasses or a helmet with a face shield.
ref: Tennessee Motorcycle Operator Manual, p. 24

prompt: When must a motorcycle's headlight be on in Tennessee?
choices: At all times while it is operated
explanation: Tennessee law requires a motorcycle's headlights to be on at all times while it is being operated.
ref: Tennessee Motorcycle Operator Manual, p. 23

prompt: Which restriction applies to a 15-year-old with a Tennessee motorcycle learner permit?
choices: May carry one passenger 18 or older
May ride only in daylight, within 20 miles of home, with no passengers
May ride on interstates with a parent following
explanation: The motorcycle learner permit limits riders to 650 cc, no passengers, no interstates, daylight hours only and a 20-mile radius of home.
ref: Tennessee Motorcycle Operator Manual, p. 5

prompt: What is the largest engine size a 15-year-old Tennessee motorcycle learner permit holder may ride?
explanation: The motorcycle learner permit limits the rider to a motorcycle with a maximum cylinder size of 650 cc.
ref: Tennessee Motorcycle Operator Manual, p. 5

prompt: A 15-year-old in Tennessee holds a Class M-Limited license for a motor-driven cycle. When and where may they ride?
choices: Only between 4 a.m. and 8 p.m. and within 7 miles of home
Only in daylight within 20 miles of home
explanation: A motor-driven cycle license issued at 15 is valid only between 4:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m. and within a seven-mile radius of the driver's home.
ref: Tennessee Motorcycle Operator Manual, p. 4

prompt: A Tennessee driver with a valid license completes a state-certified Motorcycle Rider Education Program (MREP). What does the certificate do?
choices: Nothing; all tests are still required
It waives the motorcycle knowledge and skills tests at the Driver Service Center
It waives only the vision screening
It lets them ride without a helmet
explanation: Holders of a valid Tennessee license with an MREP completion certificate are exempt from the motorcycle knowledge and skills tests. An MSF course waives only the skills test.
ref: Tennessee Motorcycle Operator Manual, p. 5

prompt: Under Tennessee's child restraint law, what must a 2-year-old who weighs 30 pounds ride in?
choices: Only a seat belt, since the child weighs over 20 pounds
An adult lap belt in the front seat
explanation: Tennessee requires children one through three years old who weigh more than 20 pounds to ride in a forward-facing child safety seat, in the back seat if possible. Children under 1 year old or under 20 pounds must ride rear-facing, and children 4 through 8 who are under 4 feet 9 inches use a booster seat.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 45

prompt: Who may legally use the emergency crossovers in the median of a Tennessee interstate?
choices: Drivers stuck in a traffic jam who want to turn back
Any driver who first comes to a full stop and checks traffic
Any vehicle with its hazard flashers turned on
Only emergency vehicles and highway maintenance crews
explanation: Emergency crossovers are only for emergency vehicles and highway maintenance crews. Using one to turn around, even after missing an exit or in a traffic jam, is dangerous and illegal; U-turns are illegal on Tennessee interstates, so drive on to the next exit.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 73

prompt: A Tennessee driver is convicted of DUI because a prescription painkiller impaired their driving. How do the penalties compare with a DUI for alcohol?
choices: They are lighter, because the drug was legally prescribed
They are the same as for an alcohol DUI
There is no penalty if the driver shows a valid prescription
Only a fine applies; the license is not affected
explanation: The Tennessee manual warns that driving under the influence of drugs, even prescription drugs, carries the same penalties as driving under the influence of alcohol. A prescription does not make impaired driving legal.
ref: Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual, p. 96
